claims.summary: For a finite matrix M with rows U and columns C, Delta(M) the least constant with sum over u of |sum over N of beta(N) M(u,N)|^2 <= Delta sum |beta|^2 for all beta. (1) If every entry has modulus 1 or 0, Delta is at least the number of nonzero entries of each row and of each column. (2) Squarefree primary n in Z[omega] prime to S, sextic symbols chi_n extended by zero; D a finite set of such n, c with c(ab) = c(a) c(b) for coprime a, b; A_u = sum over D of c(n) chi_n(u); T the ordered m-tuples of pairwise coprime elements of D, C_m their products, t(N) the number of tuples with product N. Then A_u^m = Q_u + R_u with Q_u = sum over C_m of c(N) t(N) chi_N(u). (3) If |c| = 1 on C_m and U contains u0 prime to all of D, then for M(u,N) = chi_N(u) on U x C_m: Delta(M) sum |c(N) t(N)|^2 >= |T|^2. (4) For u0 prime to all of D, c(n) = conj(chi_n(u0)) is multiplicative on coprime arguments, of modulus 1 on D, and gives A_u0 = |D|, so the sum over any U containing u0 of |A_u|^(2m) is at least |D|^(2m).
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof (test vectors for a row and a column; expansion of the power; Cauchy's inequality; one row). The obstruction of one row, standard; part (4) extends to an arbitrary row and every moment the argument with coefficients one of the entry on the twist average. It limits bounds valid for a class of coefficients, not the moment of the imported family. Read with one recalled count (|D| of order D): a bound of the form D^(m+eps) H valid for all unimodular coefficients multiplicative on coprime arguments needs H >= D^(m-eps), where the moment extraction gives no exponent below 1 - 1/(2k) less a term in eps. The imported second moment uses its coefficients and is not limited by this.
claims.rationale: Says which bounds cannot give a higher moment of the imported family with fewer rows than its length: none that holds for every unimodular coefficient function multiplicative on coprime arguments.
claims.next_action: Run the import's Gauss-sum identity on the extremal function of part (4) to say what its Poisson step uses of the Moebius function.
